newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Winter storm slows sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Winter storm slows sales.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat prices were mostly steady to lower on Tuesday and movement was slow as a winter storm dumped up to 11 inches of snow across key growing regions, cash dealers said.
"It's really slow because of the snow," a Montana dealer said. "We've got massive amounts (of snow), at least 11 inches, and the wind chill is six degrees (Farenheit)."
Snow and ice slowed truck and rail movement in the Pacific Northwest, stalling grain transport.
"We've bought some wheat but it's coming in slow because of the cold," another Montana dealer said.
In Oregon, dealers reported up to six inches of snow. Farmer selling in the area was sporadic, they said.
"They're a little bit moving here but it's pretty skimpy," one dealer said. "They're selling just as much as they have to to pay the bills in their hands."
